title: Analysis of inflammatory biomarkers and evaluation of regulatory molecular mechanisms in obstructive lung diseases (COPD and bronchial asthma) with different targeted therapies: a multicenter, prospective, longitudinal observational study.
summary:
People with chronic obstructive lung diseases such as COPD or asthma often experience reduced quality of life. Certain targeted therapies have improved disease control in certain patient groups. However, it is difficult to predict how well a specific medication will work or how the disease will progress. Research aims to better understand the molecular mechanisms of these diseases and their changes during therapy to enable more personalized treatment.

The AERO study observes patients undergoing various targeted therapies. In addition to medical data, samples such as blood, swabs, or tissue are collected to identify new biomarkers. These biomarkers could help select the best therapy before treatment begins, detect severe disease progression early, and advance research on chronic inflammatory diseases.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Female and male patients aged ≥ 18 years (at the time of written consent) with no upper age limit.
2. Written informed consent is available.
3. Confirmed diagnosis of COPD grade B or E, or severe bronchial asthma.
4. First prescription of a biologic therapy or use of ongoing inhalation therapy (initial therapy not mandatory).
5. Ability to comply with the study protocol.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Pregnant or breastfeeding mothers
2. Anemia with a hemoglobin value < 10 g/dl
3. Exclusion criteria are generally also defined by the contraindications for biologic therapies
